# px0 - Automate your recurring chores in plain English, completely local

> px0 turns a plain-English description of a recurring job into a Markdown workflow you can run, schedule, and edit. Everything lives in one directory on your machine (`~/.px0`). There is no server, no account, and no hosted state. Workflows reach 1,000+ external apps through Composio, and the model backend is a coding agent CLI you already sign into (claude, gemini, pi, or opencode).

This index is written for large language models and AI agents. It maps the px0 product, its concepts, and its command surface.

## Core resources

- [Home page](https://px0.ai): what px0 is, how a workflow gets built, and how to install it.
- [Documentation](https://docs.px0.ai): tutorials, workflow file format, CLI reference, configuration.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0): source, issues, and the install script.
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/px0/): the published `px0` distribution.

## What px0 is

- A single CLI (`px0`), installed with pipx, running entirely on the user's machine.
- A store at `~/.px0` (override with `PX0_HOME`) holding `workflows/`, `guidelines/`, `brain/`, and `output/`, all plain Markdown.
- A workflow builder: `px0 workflows new "<sentence>"` runs four passes (clarify, discover, confirm, plan) and writes a workflow file.
- A scheduler: `px0 daemon install` picks launchd, systemd, or cron, fires due workflows, and backfills fires the machine slept through.
- A brain: `px0 brain add` ingests URLs, PDFs, docs, and video transcripts; `px0 brain ask` answers questions over them with citations.
- An MCP server: `px0 mcp serve` exposes the brain and the workflow list over the Model Context Protocol, so an agent can query and run them without being told how the CLI works.
- A provenance trail: every run records its inputs, the guideline versions inlined, and every tool call; `px0 runs why <run-id>` explains how an output came to be.

## What px0 is not

- Not a hosted service, SaaS dashboard, or prompt registry.
- Not an SDK you embed in an application.
- Not a direct-API LLM client: it shells out to a coding agent CLI as its model backend.
